General Background
In the mid-1960's Milwaukee County experienced the construction of segments of its county freeway system. This system helped alleviate traffic congestion on its already overburdened local street system and in turn drastically reduced travel times to various locations within the county. Travel time from the Milwaukee Central Business District to General Mitchell Field was also reduced.
Since the inception of planning for Interstate Routes

I-94 and I-894 in Milwaukee County, the concept of more direct access
to General Mitchell Field to further reduce travel effort to it
has been under discussion.
General Mitchell Field is Wisconsin's principal airport which services the southeastern area of the state and is conveniently located 6-1/2 miles directly south of downtown Milwaukee. The 2,058 acre airport complex is located east of Howell Avenue, on STH 38. See figure 4.
Initially, it was thought that the vehicular traffic desiring access to General Mitchell Field would be able to use the Interstate System and exit at interchange facilities in the vicinity of the airport onto the existing local street system to reach the airport.
These access routes, however, are not direct routes and involve considerable indirection with an average of 2.4 miles of travel over the local street system.
In order to have a more direct access route to General Mitchell Field, Milwaukee County prior to the actual construction of the North-South Freeway, I-94, requested access to the Interstate System at Grange Avenue. The FHWA denied this at the time.
